title: B.C. BigTree Registry
summary: Explore where 1,061 living registry trees are mapped, then compare the snapshot by tree type, height, trunk diameter, and tree score.
sourceNote: This project normalizes the BC BigTree Registry GeoJSON snapshot supplied with the BC Forest Map source archive. UBC's Registry Reports page remains the source of record and publishes the living-tree registry as spreadsheet and CSV files. The snapshot is shown as a reference rather than a live registry feed.
details: Every record has point coordinates, but 79 of 1,061 records lack the separate descriptive location field. Those records still provide a nearest town.
Eighteen records share a coordinate with another tree, so some points overlap at province-wide scales.
Height is available for 928 trees, diameter at breast height (DBH) for 1,059, and tree score for 696. Every metric map shows unavailable values explicitly rather than dropping those trees.
UBC asks visitors to respect private property, use caution on logging roads, file a trip plan in remote areas, and view trees from afar to protect roots and vegetation.

scenes.label: Locations
scenes.title: Every tree has coordinates, but not every record has a named location
scenes.text: All 1,061 records can be placed on the map. The separate location field is present for 982 trees; the remaining 79 still provide a nearest town. Some trees share coordinates and therefore overlap until the map is zoomed in.
scenes.focus: Mapped points and descriptive location coverage

callout.label: Nearest town only
callout.detail: Mapped coordinates are present, but the descriptive location field is blank.

scenes.label: Tree types
scenes.title: Conifers account for most records in the supplied snapshot
scenes.text: Nine hundred mapped trees are conifers and 161 are broadleaves. Western redcedar, Sitka spruce, and coastal Douglas-fir are the most frequently represented common names.

callout.label: Conifer share
callout.detail: About 85 percent of mapped registry trees.

scenes.label: Height
scenes.title: The tallest recorded tree in the snapshot reaches 96 metres
scenes.text: Height is available for 928 trees and unavailable for 133. Carmanah Giant, a Sitka spruce near Youbou, has the highest recorded value in this snapshot.

callout.label: Maximum recorded height
callout.detail: Carmanah Giant · Sitka spruce · Registry ID 87.

scenes.label: Diameter
scenes.title: Trunk diameter reveals a different pattern than height
scenes.text: DBH is available for 1,059 of the 1,061 trees. The widest recorded trunk is a western redcedar near Youbou at 5.96 metres, while the median recorded DBH is 2.43 metres.

scenes.label: Tree score
scenes.title: Tree score combines dimensions into another view of significance
scenes.text: A tree score is supplied for 696 records and unavailable for 365. Cheewhat Giant, a western redcedar near Youbou, has the highest recorded score in the snapshot.

callout.label: Maximum recorded score
callout.detail: Cheewhat Giant · western redcedar · Registry ID 84.
